page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v6 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the Esv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data shows strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1975.0 and a strong text processing score of 2658.0, both placing in the top 25% of tested servers. In contrast, multi-core performance is average, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7558.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 7972.24. Memory bandwidth is measured at 626.49 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 42.29 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, while the Passmark memory score is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%. For language model workloads, the server achieves a strong text generation speed of 302.13 tokens/sec on a small 135M model, but drops to a weak 8.06 tokens/sec for text generation on a medium 7B model.

Given its high memory density of 16.0 GB per core alongside dedicated CPU resources, the E16-8s_v6 offers a qualitative cost-efficiency profile suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. The lack of local storage means storage requirements must be met via external Premium Storage. This server is best suited for memory-optimized workloads such as relational databases, caching layers, and lightweight data processing tasks where RAM capacity is prioritized over high core counts.
